Question 11 mark

Consider the following recurrence relation.

A0 = 3,     An+1 = −2An + 3

The first four terms of this recurrence relation are

A.−3, 9, −15, 33, … ✓
B.3, −3, 9, −15, … ✓
C.3, −12, 18, −42, … ✓
D.−12, 18, −42, 78, … ✓
E.3, −3, 21, 45, … ✓
A1 = −2 × 3 + 3 = −3; A2 = −2 × −3 + 3 = 9; A3 = −2 × 9 + 3 = −15
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q3
Question 21 mark

Consider the following recurrence relation

R0 = −1,     Rn+1 = 0.25Rn + 2

The first five terms of the sequence created by this relation, correct to two decimal places, are

A.1.75, 2.44, 2.61, 2.65, 2.66 ✓
B.−1, 1.75, 2.43, 2.61, 2.65 ✓
C.−1, 1.75, 2.44, 2.60, 2.66 ✓
D.1.75, 2.43, 2.60, 2.65, 2.66 ✓
E.−1, 1.75, 2.44, 2.61, 2.65 ✓
R0 = −1 is the first term. CAS: 1.75, 2.4375, 2.60938, 2.65234 → −1, 1.75, 2.44, 2.61, 2.65 (careful with the rounding).
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q6

7B

Linear growth and decay: simple interest, flat rate and unit cost depreciation

Done
Date
Multiple choiceCircle one answer. 3 marks
Question 41 mark

A printer was purchased for $1200. After three years, the printer has a value of $765.

On average, 1740 pages were printed every year.

The value of the printer was depreciated using a unit cost method of depreciation.

The depreciation in the value of the printer, per page printed, is closest to

A.5 cents. ✓
B.6 cents. ✓
C.7 cents. ✓
D.8 cents. ✓
E.9 cents. ✓
1200 − 765 = 435 over three years = 145 per year; 145 ÷ 1740 = $0.0833 ≈ 8 cents per page.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q2
Question 51 mark

Five years after a car was purchased, it is worth $26 000. On average, it travels 22 000 kilometres per year.

If it depreciates on a unit cost basis at 14 cents per kilometre, its purchase price was closest to

A.$10 600 ✓
B.$29 080 ✓
C.$41 400 ✓
D.$56 000 ✓
E.$136 000 ✓
22 000 × 0.14 × 5 = $15 400 depreciation; 26 000 + 15 400 = $41 400.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q8
Question 61 mark

The graph below shows the value of an asset that was purchased for $6000. Its value decreases on a flat rate basis each year.

How much had the asset depreciated by after four years?

A.$3800 ✓
B.$2200 ✓
C.$1650 ✓
D.$550 ✓
E.$412.50 ✓
After three years: 6000 − 4350 = $1650, which is $550 per year. Four years × 550 = $2200.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.6 Q12

Rules for the nth term of linear growth and decay

Done
Date
Multiple choiceCircle one answer. 2 marks
Question 71 mark

A motorbike was purchased for $23 200.

After three years the motorbike has a value of $16 990.

On average, the motorbike travelled 22 500 kilometres every year during those three years.

The value of the motorbike was depreciated using a unit cost method of depreciation.

The value of the motorbike, in dollars, after n kilometres are travelled, Vn, can be modelled by the rule

A.Vn+1 = Vn − 0.092n ✓
B.Vn+1 = 23 200 − 0.092Vn ✓
C.Vn = 23 200 − 0.092n ✓
D.Vn = 23 200 − 6200n ✓
E.Vn+1 = 23 200 − 0.092n ✓
23 200 − 16 990 = 6210; 6210 ÷ (22 500 × 3) = 0.092 per km. Rule Vn = V0 − nD = 23 200 − 0.092n.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q1
Question 81 mark

An appliance is purchased for $486. It depreciates using the rule shown below, where n represents the number of time periods.

Vn = 486 − 14n

This model of depreciation shown is

A.reducing balance depreciation, at a rate of depreciation of 14% per time period. ✓
B.flat rate depreciation, at a rate of depreciation of $14 per time period. ✓
C.reducing balance loan, at a rate of depreciation of 14% per time period. ✓
D.reducing balance depreciation, at a rate of depreciation of $14 per time period. ✓
E.flat rate depreciation, at a rate of depreciation of 14% per time period. ✓
Vn = V0 − Dn is flat rate, with D the dollar amount ($14). Reducing balance rules have the form Vn = Rn × V0.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.6 Q14
Short answerShow your working. 6 marks
Question 93 marks

Casey’s first motorbike had a purchase price of $37 000.

After five years, the value of the motorbike was $29 600.

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q1
aLet Cn be the value of the motorbike n years after it was purchased.
Assume that the value of the motorbike has depreciated using the flat rate method of depreciation.
Write a recurrence relation, in terms of Cn and Cn+1, that models the value of the motorbike.2 marks
(37 000 − 29 600) ÷ 5 = 1480 per year. C0 = 37 000,   Cn+1 = Cn − 1480
bThe motorbike has travelled an average of 4000 km in each of the five years since it was purchased.
Assume that the value of the motorbike has been depreciated using the unit cost method of depreciation.
By how much is the value of the motorbike reduced per kilometre travelled?1 mark
Rule Vn = V0 − nD: 35 520 = 37 000 − 4000 × D (one year) → D = $0.37: 37 cents per kilometre (a unit is required).
Question 103 marks

Saskia invests $3050 in an account earning 12% per annum on a flat rate basis.

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.10 Q9
a iWrite a calculation that shows that the interest earned each year is $366.1 mark
0.12 × 3050 = 366 (or 12/100 × 3050)
iiWrite the rule that gives the balance of the investment, Bn, in dollars after n years.1 mark
Bn = 3050 + 366n
iiiHow long until the balance is $7076?1 mark
7076 = 3050 + 366n → n = 11 years
7D

Geometric growth and decay: compound interest and reducing balance depreciation

Done
Date
Multiple choiceCircle one answer. 4 marks
Question 111 mark

Which of the following recurrence relations represents geometric decay?

A.C0 = 100,   Cn+1 = 0.84 × Cn + 100 ✓
B.C0 = 100,   Cn+1 = 1.684 × Cn ✓
C.C0 = 100,   Cn+1 = 0.684 × Cn ✓
D.C0 = 100,   Cn+1 = 1.684 × Cn + 25 ✓
E.C0 = 100,   Cn+1 = Cn + 345 ✓
Multiplying by a number less than 1 (and adding nothing) is geometric decay. A mixes geometric decay with arithmetic growth; B is geometric growth; D mixes geometric and arithmetic growth; E is arithmetic growth.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q4
Question 121 mark

Consider the following graph.

Which of the following could be modelled by the graph?

A.a reducing balance loan with regular payments ✓
B.a flat rate loan with regular payments ✓
C.a compound interest account ✓
D.an interest only loan ✓
E.a simple interest investment with regular payments ✓
The value increases, so it is an investment (not A, B, D). It increases by slightly more each month (not by the same amount, as E would): compounding interest.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4 Q5
Question 131 mark

The graph below shows the value, Vn, of an investment as it increases over eight years.

Which one of the following investments does this graph best represent?

A.a simple interest investment earning interest at a rate of 10% per annum ✓
B.a compound interest investment earning interest at a rate of 10% per annum, with a yearly payment ✓
C.a perpetuity earning interest at a rate of 103% per annum. ✓
D.an annuity investment earning interest at a rate of 10% per annum, with a yearly withdrawal. ✓
E.a compound interest investment earning interest at a rate of 10% per annum, with a yearly withdrawal ✓
The balance does not increase by the same amount each year (not A or C). It keeps increasing, so no withdrawals are being taken (not D or E).
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q7
Question 141 mark

[Adapted: Insight’s question does not give the lounge suite’s details; they are taken from Insight’s worked solution.] A lounge suite is bought for $4500 and depreciates on a reducing balance basis at 9.4% per annum.

When using recursion, which one of the following calculations determines the value of the lounge suite at the end of the third year?

A.0.906 × 4077 = 3693.76 ✓
B.3690 − 405 = 3285 ✓
C.1.09 × 4905 = 5346.45 ✓
D.0.906 × 3693.76 = 3346.55 ✓
E.1.09 × 5346.45 = 5827.63 ✓
V0 = 4500, Vn+1 = 0.906Vn: 4077, 3693.76, then 0.906 × 3693.76 = 3346.55. A is the end of the second year; B is flat rate; C and E are growth.
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q11
Short answerShow your working. 19 marks
Question 156 marks

Jonathan purchased a car for $24 990.

The value of Jonathan’s car was depreciated using the unit cost method of depreciation.

The value of the car, in dollars, after n kilometres, Vn, can be modelled by the rule shown below.

V0 = 24 990,     Vn = 24 990 − 0.0015n

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.4–5 Q2
aShow that the value of the car after 20 000 kilometres is $24 960.2 marks
Vn = 24 990 − 0.0015 × 20 000 = 24 960
bWhat is the cost, in cents per kilometre, that Jonathan’s car is being depreciated?1 mark
0.0015 × 100 = 0.15 cents per kilometre
cIf Jonathan were to use the flat rate method of depreciation, it would take him 3 years to depreciate the car to $23 191.
Find the annual flat rate of depreciation. Give your answer as a percentage. Round your answer to one decimal place.1 mark
24 990 − 23 191 = 1799; 1799 ÷ 3 = 599.67 per year; 599.67 ÷ 24 990 × 100 = 2.39964% ≈ 2.4%
dIt was suggested to Jonathan that a reducing balance method of depreciation may be more appropriate to depreciate the value of his car.
If the car is depreciated at a reducing balance rate of 5.8% per annum, write down a recurrence relation, in terms of A0, An+1 and An, for the value of Jonathan’s car, in dollars, after n years.2 marks
R = 1 − 5.8/100 = 0.942.   A0 = 24 990,   An+1 = 0.942 × An
Question 166 marks

Casey has opened a simple interest savings account in order to save money to buy a new motorbike. Interest is paid monthly into this account. The amount of money in the savings account after n years, Vn, can be modelled by the recurrence relation shown below.

V0 = 6000,     Vn+1 = Vn + 216

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.6–7 Q4
aHow much money did Casey initially deposit in his savings account?1 mark
$6000 (V0)
bWhat is the annual percentage interest rate for this savings account?2 marks
216 ÷ 6000 × 100 = 3.6% p.a.
c iThe amount of money in the account after n years, Vn, can also be determined using a rule.
Complete the rule by writing the appropriate numbers in the boxes provided below.
Vn = 6000 + 216 × n
1 mark
iiHow much money will be in Casey’s savings account after 5 years?1 mark
V5 = 6000 + 216 × 5 = $7080
dCasey decides to compare a compound interest savings account to his savings in the simple interest account. He invests $6000 at an interest rate of 5.4% compounding annually. The amount of money in the savings account after n years, Vn, can be modelled by the recurrence relation shown below.
V0 = 6000,     Vn+1 = 1.054 × Vn
Use recursion to write down calculations that show that the amount of money in Casey’s compound interest savings account after 2 years, V2, will be $6665.50.1 mark
V1 = 1.054 × 6000 = 6324;   V2 = 1.054 × 6324 = 6665.496 ≈ $6665.50
Question 174 marks

Jason is a personal trainer who has purchased a large piece of equipment for his home gym.

The value of Jason’s equipment is depreciated using the reducing balance method.

The value of the equipment, in dollars, after n years, Vn, can be modelled by the recurrence relation shown below.

V0 = 12 000,     Vn+1 = 0.92Vn

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.8 Q6
aWrite down a calculation, using the value of the equipment after 4 years, to show that the value of Jason’s equipment after 5 years, V5, is $7908.98.1 mark
CAS recursion: V4 = 8596.72.   V5 = 0.92 × 8596.72 = 7908.98
bAfter how many years will the value of Jason’s equipment first fall below $7500?1 mark
V5 = 7908.98, V6 = 7276.26: after 6 years
c iJason has another option for depreciation of his equipment.
He can depreciate the value of his equipment using unit cost depreciation, where a ‘unit’ is counted each time the equipment is used for a workout.
In the first two years, Jason completed 1400 workouts.
The value of his equipment after this time was $10 850.
What is the unit cost of depreciation for Jason’s equipment?
Give your answer to the nearest cent.1 mark
12 000 − 10 850 = 1150; 1150 ÷ 1400 = $0.82 (82 cents)
iiLet Vn be the value of the equipment after n workouts, in dollars.
Write down a rule in terms of Vn that could be used to model the value of the equipment using this unit cost depreciation.1 mark
Vn = 12 000 − 0.82n
Question 183 marks

Saskia buys a commercial washing machine for her laundromat business. The value of the washing machine after n years is shown by the equations below:

V0 = 3875    Vn+1 = Vn − 410

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.9–10 Q8
a iShowing recursive calculations, determine the value of the washing machine after two years.1 mark
V1 = 3875 − 410 = 3465;   V2 = 3465 − 410 = $3055
iiWhat is the annual flat rate of depreciation?
Write your answer as a percentage rounded to two decimal places.1 mark
410 ÷ 3875 × 100 = 10.58%
bAn alternative model of depreciation is that the machine depreciates by $800 immediately upon purchase, then depreciates at 6% per year on a reducing balance basis.
What is the value of the machine after three years using this method?
Round your answer to the nearest dollar.1 mark
3875 − 800 = 3075; 3075 × 0.943 = 2554.05 ≈ $2554 (or recursion V0 = 3075, Vn+1 = 0.94Vn)

Rules for the nth term of geometric growth and decay

Done
Date
Multiple choiceCircle one answer. 2 marks
Question 191 mark

An asset was purchased for $124 000. It depreciates on a reducing balance basis at a rate of 5.6% per annum.

The value of the asset after 6 years is shown by the rule

A.V6 = 124 000 × (0.944 × 6) ✓
B.V6 = 124 000 − (1.056 × 6) ✓
C.V6 = 124 000 − (0.944 × 6) ✓
D.V6 = 124 000 − (0.056)6 ✓
E.V6 = 124 000 × (0.944)6 ✓
Vn = V0 × (1 − r/100)n = 124 000 × (1 − 5.6/100)6 = 124 000 × 0.9446
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q9
Question 201 mark

[Adapted: Insight’s question does not give the lounge suite’s details; they are taken from Insight’s worked solution.] A lounge suite is bought for $4500 and depreciates on a reducing balance basis at 9.4% per annum.

A rule for the value of a lounge suite after n years is

A.Vn = 1.094 × 4500 ✓
B.Vn+1 = 0.906Vn ✓
C.Vn+1 = 0.906n × 4500 ✓
D.Vn = 0.906n × 4500 ✓
E.Vn = 1.094n × 4500 ✓
Vn = (1 − 9.4/100)n × 4500 = 0.906n × 4500. B and C use Vn+1 (recurrence notation, not a rule); A and E use 1 + 9.4/100 (growth).
Insight GM1 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5 Q10

Question 213 marks

Alison withdraws $5000 from her account to purchase a new photocopier for her business. The value of the photocopier will be depreciated using the reducing balance method. The value of Alison’s photocopier, in dollars, after n years, Cn, can be modelled by the recurrence relation shown below.

C0 = 5000,     Cn+1 = R × Cn

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.5–6 Q3
aThe annual rate of depreciation for this photocopier is 18%.
What is the value of R in the recurrence relation?1 mark
R = 1 − 18/100 = 0.82
bHow much has the photocopier depreciated in value after five years of use?1 mark
5000 × 0.825 = 1853.70; 5000 − 1853.70 = $3146.30
cThe value of the photocopier after one year of use is $4100. Alison’s company prints approximately 35 000 pages per month on this photocopier. Alison chooses to calculate the depreciation of her photocopier using unit cost depreciation.
By how much does the photocopier depreciate per page, using this method?
Give your answer in cents to one decimal place.1 mark
900 depreciation in one year; 35 000 × 12 = 420 000 pages; 900 ÷ 420 000 = $0.002143 = 0.2 cents per page
Question 225 marks

Alison invests her money into a savings account that will pay compound interest every month. The balance of Alison’s account, after n months, Vn, can be modelled by the recurrence relation shown below.

V0 = 8000,     Vn+1 = 1.00225 Vn

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.7–8 Q5
aWhat is the annual interest rate for Alison’s savings account?1 mark
Solve 1.00225 = 1 + (r/12)/100 → r = 2.7% per annum
b iRecursion can be used to calculate the balance of the account after each month.
Write down a calculation to show that the balance in the account after two months, V2, is $8036.04.1 mark
V1 = 1.00225 × 8000 = 8018;   V2 = 1.00225 × 8018 = 8036.04
iiAfter how many months will the balance of Alison’s account first exceed $8500?1 mark
CAS recursion: after 27 months
cA rule of the form Vn = a × bn can be used to determine the balance of Alison’s account after n months.
Write the rule for Alison’s investment below.1 mark
Vn = 8000 × 1.00225n
dThe value of Alison’s investment after 12 months is $8219 when rounded to the nearest dollar.
What is the equivalent flat rate interest rate, per annum, for Alison’s investment?
Round your answer to two decimal places.1 mark
Interest = 8219 − 8000 = 219; 219 = 8000 × r × 1 ÷ 100 → r = 219 ÷ 8000 × 100 = 2.74%
Question 234 marks

Jo invests $80 000 at a simple interest rate of 3.4% per annum.

Her brother Anthony invests the same amount of money in an account earning 3.25% per annum, compounding annually.

Insight GM2 U3 Recursion and Financial Modelling p.9 Q7
aHow much interest does Jo earn each year?1 mark
0.034 × 80 000 = $2720
bWrite a recurrence relation to model the value of Anthony’s investment in terms of V0, Vn+1 and Vn.1 mark
V0 = 80 000,   Vn+1 = 1.0325Vn
cWhat is the value of Anthony’s investment after eight years?1 mark
V8 = 1.03258 × 80 000 = $103 326.20 (or Finance Solver)
dAfter how many years will Anthony’s investment be larger than Jo’s?1 mark
Jo: 80 000, 82 720, 85 440, 88 160, 90 880. Anthony: 80 000, 82 600, 85 284.50, 88 056.25, 90 918.07. After four years.
